**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics Paper 2 (0765/2), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical Formulae Booklets published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.
incertitudes: Question 5 (a) : « the point of intersection of C1 and C2 » (singulier imprime) : les deux cercles se coupent en DEUX points, (1, 2) et (9/5, 18/5) ; le corrige prend le cercle C3 du faisceau engendre par C1 et C2 qui passe par le centre (3, 2) de C1, ce qui le fixe de maniere unique.

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the circles $C_1: x^2 + y^2 - 6x - 4y + 9 = 0$ and $C_2: x^2 + y^2 - 2x - 6y + 9 = 0$, find the equation of the circle $C_3$ which passes through the centre of $C_1$ and through the point of intersection of $C_1$ and $C_2$. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Centres and radii.** Write $S_1 = x^2 + y^2 - 6x - 4y + 9$ and $S_2 = x^2 + y^2 - 2x - 6y + 9$.

- $C_1$: $(x-3)^2 + (y-2)^2 = 9 + 4 - 9 = 4$, centre $(3, 2)$, radius $2$.
- $C_2$: $(x-1)^2 + (y-3)^2 = 1 + 9 - 9 = 1$, centre $(1, 3)$, radius $1$.

**Points of intersection.** Subtracting, $S_1 - S_2 = -4x + 2y = 0$, so $y = 2x$. Substitute in $S_2 = 0$: $x^2 + 4x^2 - 2x - 12x + 9 = 0$, i.e. $5x^2 - 14x + 9 = 0$, i.e. $(5x - 9)(x - 1) = 0$. The circles meet at $(1, 2)$ and $\left(\dfrac95, \dfrac{18}{5}\right)$ (the distance between the centres is $\sqrt5$, which lies between $|2 - 1| = 1$ and $2 + 1 = 3$, so two intersection points are expected).

**The family of circles through the intersection points.** Every circle through both points has an equation of the form

$$S_1 + \mu S_2 = 0 \qquad (\mu \ne -1).$$

It must pass through the centre of $C_1$, $(3, 2)$. Evaluate: $S_1(3,2) = 9 + 4 - 18 - 8 + 9 = -4$ and $S_2(3,2) = 9 + 4 - 6 - 12 + 9 = 4$. So $-4 + 4\mu = 0$, hence $\mu = 1$.

$$S_1 + S_2 = 2x^2 + 2y^2 - 8x - 10y + 18 = 0.$$

Divide by 2:

$$\boxed{C_3:\ x^2 + y^2 - 4x - 5y + 9 = 0}$$

Its centre is $\left(2, \dfrac52\right)$ and its radius is $\sqrt{4 + \dfrac{25}{4} - 9} = \dfrac{\sqrt5}{2}$.

**Check.** $(3,2)$: $9 + 4 - 12 - 10 + 9 = 0$. $(1,2)$: $1 + 4 - 4 - 10 + 9 = 0$. $\left(\dfrac95, \dfrac{18}{5}\right)$: $\dfrac{81 + 324}{25} - \dfrac{36}{5} - 18 + 9 = 16.2 - 7.2 - 9 = 0$. All three points lie on $C_3$.

questions.enonce_markdown: For the circle $C_1: x^2 + y^2 - 6x - 4y + 9 = 0$, find the equations of the two tangents from the origin to $C_1$ and the length of each tangent. (7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
$C_1$ has centre $P(3, 2)$ and radius $r = 2$ (from $(x-3)^2 + (y-2)^2 = 4$). The origin $O$ is outside the circle because $S_1(0,0) = 9 > 0$ (equivalently $OP = \sqrt{13} > 2$), so there are two tangents from $O$.

**Equations of the tangents.** The line $x = 0$ is not a tangent (the distance from $P$ to it is $3 \ne 2$), so a tangent through $O$ has the form $y = mx$, i.e. $mx - y = 0$. It touches $C_1$ when the distance from the centre to the line equals the radius:

$$\frac{|3m - 2|}{\sqrt{m^2 + 1}} = 2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad (3m - 2)^2 = 4(m^2 + 1).$$

$$9m^2 - 12m + 4 = 4m^2 + 4 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 5m^2 - 12m = 0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad m(5m - 12) = 0.$$

So $m = 0$ or $m = \dfrac{12}{5}$:

$$\boxed{y = 0 \quad\text{and}\quad 12x - 5y = 0\ \ \left(y = \tfrac{12}{5}x\right)}$$

(Check: the $x$-axis is at distance $2$ from the centre $(3, 2)$, equal to the radius, and touches the circle at $(3, 0)$.)

**Length of each tangent.** The radius to the point of contact $T$ is perpendicular to the tangent, so triangle $OTP$ is right-angled at $T$ and

$$OT^2 = OP^2 - r^2 = (3^2 + 2^2) - 2^2 = 9, \qquad OT = 3.$$

This is the same as $\sqrt{S_1(0,0)} = \sqrt9 = 3$. The two tangent segments from an external point are equal in length, so each has length

$$\boxed{3 \text{ units}}$$

(Check: the point of contact on $y = 0$ is $(3, 0)$, at distance $3$ from $O$; the point of contact on $12x - 5y = 0$ is the foot of the perpendicular from $P$, namely $\left(\dfrac{15}{13}, \dfrac{36}{13}\right)$, at distance $\dfrac{\sqrt{225 + 1296}}{13} = \dfrac{39}{13} = 3$ from $O$.)
